title: JPMorganChase's new community outlook survey reveals how Philadelphia area residents view the local economy, housing, careers and their personal finances

# JPMorganChase's new community outlook survey reveals how Philadelphia area residents view the local economy, housing, careers and their personal finances


Nearly half of Philadelphia residents — 47% — name peace of mind and financial security as one of their top three financial goals, even as most residents lean toward a cautious read on the local economy


Philadelphia


---


November 23, 2026


JPMorganChase today released local findings from its first-ever Community Outlook survey of the Philadelphia area, measuring how residents view their financial lives, their communities, and their aspirations.


According to the findings, almost half (47%) of Philadelphia residents rank peace of mind and financial security among their top three financial goals — the single most-cited priority in the city — offering a detailed portrait of how the community is navigating economic conditions, cost-of-living pressures, career decisions, and its evolving definition of the American Dream. That focus on stability stands out against a more guarded view of the wider economy: 27% of residents describe the local economy as somewhat downbeat and 20% as very downbeat, while 41% say it is declining compared with a few years ago.


"Philadelphians are telling us that stability and peace of mind come first, and they're taking real steps to protect it," said Rob Melchionni, Philadelphia Region Manager for Commercial Banking and Co-Chair of the Market Leadership Team, JPMorganChase. "Our job is to meet residents where they are — helping them build savings, pay down debt, and plan for the future with confidence right here at home."


## Views on the local economy & achieving financial dreams


Residents shared their top financial goals, their outlook on home ownership, and how broader economic conditions are shaping their personal finances. The survey also captured sentiment around buying versus renting and what the American Dream means.


- Philly residents want to build resiliency and plan for the future: Almost half


(47%) said peace of mind and financial security is among their most important financial priorities, followed by retirement and long-term savings at 34% and building an emergency fund at 27%.
- How Philly residents define the American Dream:


Over half (51%) chose financial independence as best defining the American Dream, closely followed by owning a home (48%) and being able to afford day-to-day expenses without stress (48%).
- Scams remain a concern for some residents:


32% reported having been targeted by a scam call, and 26% by an online scam, in a section examining the financial hardships residents have faced.


As part of its[American Dream Initiative](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/newsroom/press-releases/2026/american-dream-initiative-doubling-down-on-community-banking) , JPMorganChase is expanding its community banking efforts to help more people build the knowledge and confidence to manage their money, increasing financial health education programming with the goal of reaching 5 million people. The multi-year effort to expand economic opportunity also focuses on advancing small business growth, increasing affordable housing, improving financial health, helping people secure good jobs, expanding access to quality healthcare and strengthening local institutions in Philadelphia and communities across the country.


"Philadelphia residents are managing real cost-of-living pressures with resolve, prioritizing security and taking concrete steps to protect it," said Tanyika Rickard, Community Manager in Philadelphia for Chase. "We're committed to standing alongside this community — expanding access to financial education, tools, and guidance that help residents reach their goals."


## Housing & cost of living changing spending habits


The survey examined where residents are tightening their budgets, where spending has increased, and how they expect to spend during the upcoming holiday season.


- Brushing up on cooking skills but spending more on the ingredients:


55% of Philadelphia residents have cut back on dining out, the most common category for reduced spending, followed by entertainment at 42%. While 39% reported increased spending on groceries over the past year, more than any other category.
- Tightening the wallet this holiday season:


Nearly half (49%) plan to spend less on travel this holiday season compared to last year, and 46% plan to spend less on gifts.
- The significance of owning your home:


61% of residents agreed that home ownership is important for financial stability (30% strongly agree, 31% somewhat agree), even as many see it as increasingly hard to reach in today's market. While 47% said renting makes more financial sense than owning a home for some people, reflecting a pragmatic view of today's conditions.


The conversation around affordability continues to be top of mind for communities, and to help address this, JPMorganChase’s[American Dream Initiative](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/newsroom/press-releases/2026/american-dream-initiative-announcement) aims to improve affordability for hundreds of thousands of renters and buyers through increased housing supply and homeownership opportunities across the U.S.


## Views of the local job market are mixed


Amid a job market with a moderate amount of opportunity, as described by half of Philadelphia residents, 37% said it is hard to get a job.


When it comes to entrepreneurship, 34% said they currently own a business or plan to start one within the next two years (14% currently operate a business; 20% plan to start one), most often motivated by passion, cited by 35% as the biggest influence on their decision.


## Philly residents feel the impact of local news


The survey explored how closely residents follow economic news, where they source information about their local economy, and whether that coverage has influenced major life decisions.


Sixty-nine percent of Philadelphia residents said they follow local economic news and coverage at least somewhat closely (20% very closely, 49% somewhat closely). While over half (58%) get their news from local TV news, the most-used source, ahead of social media platforms at 39%.


Meanwhile, 68% said local news coverage of the economy has influenced a financial or life decision, including 29% who thought about saving more and 25% who were prompted to save more money.


For more than 155 years, JPMC has served the Greater Philadelphia area – helping make the American Dream attainable for more residents by supporting job creation, expanding opportunity and helping families thrive. We’re building on our shared history with[new support](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/newsroom/press-releases/2026/24-million-strengthening-shipbuilding-philadelphia) for the Philadelphia Navy Yard and the network of suppliers, manufacturers and skilled workers who power the region’s industrial strength. Across Philadelphia, we’re investing in local businesses, training and career pathways and tools for stronger household finances, expanding to nearly 100 total branches across the region by 2027.


## About the survey & methodology


The Community Outlook survey was conducted by Morning Consult on behalf of JPMorganChase, measuring how residents view their financial lives, their communities, and their aspirations. Interviews were conducted online between August 24 and September 11, 2026, among a total of 7,800 U.S. adults ages 18 and older, split evenly across 13 metropolitan areas: Boston, Washington, D.C., Miami, Philadelphia, Columbus, Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas/Fort Worth, Seattle, the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, and Birmingham. Results carry a margin of error of approximately ±4.0 percentage points at the 95% confidence level, and wider for subgroups. Figures for Philadelphia reflect responses from approximately 602 residents in the Philadelphia metropolitan area, including Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington, PA-NJ-DE-MD. Because several cross-market differences fall within the margin of error, some readings are described as directional rather than definitive.
